items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: My first group was called the Afro-Classic Ensemble. Ron Carter was in it.

ctx.x: That shows you how I felt about this. I’m trying to preserve it. It’s been 41 years.
It doesn’t seem like it. My first group was called the Afro-Classic Ensemble. Ron Carter was in it. I think Freddie Waits. Is Freddie Waits on that?

items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And when I was there, it was me, either Ben Riley or Billy Cobham and Frank Russell, Hubert Laws and we did several of those three, four day tours, you know.

ctx.x: Talk about Roland for a minute.

Again, another one of my friends who's gone way too soon. He had a group called the New York Jazz Quartet and several different personalities over the years that he had this group. And when I was there, it was me, either Ben Riley or Billy Cobham and Frank Russell, Hubert Laws and we did several of those three, four day tours, you know. I did some Japanese tours with Roland, with my band. He never ceased to amaze me how he would come up with these ideas and still have the sound with the Chopin-type technique to…
Richard Pratt was in that group?
